title: Horizontal pasting with the normalized single-module tensor counits
statement: Let X,S,Y,T,Z,U be schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let f:X\to S, g:T\to S, h:U\to T, p:Y\to X, q:Y\to T, t:Z\to Y, r:Z\to U and p_0:Z\to X satisfy pf=qg, tq=rh and tp=p_0. For an O_X-module G [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], let δ_1:Lg^*Rf_*(G[0])\to Rq_*((p^*G)[0]), δ_2:Lh^*Rq_*((p^*G)[0])\to Rr_*((t^*p^*G)[0]), and δ_0:L(hg)^*Rf_*(G[0])\to Rr_*((p_0^*G)[0]) be the specified single-degree base-change composites [def-weil-pbc-single-degree-module-base-change-composite]. Let e:t^*p^*G\xrightarrow{\sim}p_0^*G be inverse normalized tensor composition [def-pc-module-pullback] followed by transport along tp=p_0. Let c:Lh^*Lg^*\xrightarrow{\sim}L(hg)^* be the composition pinned by the same derived counits [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-pullback-composition]. Then Lh^*(δ_1) followed by δ_2 and Rr_*(e[0]) equals c followed by δ_0. No square is assumed cartesian and no flatness or base-change invertibility is assumed.

proof.text: Apply the derived horizontal pasting theorem to G[0], before applying any single-module counit.

Coefficient naturality moves the first single-module counit through the second mate. Evaluate the factorization for the composition-pinned counits on the homotopy single complex. The degreewise single-complex composition identity identifies its termwise map with inverse normalized tensor composition. Uniqueness of normalized tensor adjunctions identifies the tensor compositor with the mate used in that factorization. The pinned single-module comparison is the explicit construction supplied in the top-cohomology module. Use the existing named pinned composition and additive comparison; package the fixed counits behind definition equations and perform the single-complex calculation first for abstract additive functors.

Cancel the inverse derived-composition factor supplied by pasting against that single-complex factorization. Functoriality of Rr_* combines the coefficient maps. Substitute tp=p_0 and use proof irrelevance for the square equations.

theorem tensorSingleBaseChange_pasting
    {X S Y T Z U : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : T ⟶ S) (h : U ⟶ T)
    (p : Y ⟶ X) (q : Y ⟶ T) (t : Z ⟶ Y) (r : Z ⟶ U) (p₀ : Z ⟶ X)
    (hs : p ≫ f = q ≫ g) (hi : t ≫ q = r ≫ h) (hp : t ≫ p = p₀)
    (ho : p₀ ≫ f = r ≫ (h ≫ g)) (G : X.Modules) :
    letI : ∀ {V W : Scheme.{u}} (k : V ⟶ W),
      (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback k).Additive :=
      fun {_ _} k ↦ Scheme.Modules.canonicalTensorPullbackAdditive.{u, w} k
    let e := ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullbackSectionComp t p).symm.app G) ≪≫
      eqToIso (congrArg (fun k ↦ (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback k).obj G) hp)
    (derivedPullback h).map (singleDegreeBaseChangeComposite f g p q hs 0 G) ≫
        singleDegreeBaseChangeComposite q h t r hi 0
          ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback p).obj G) ≫
        (schemeDerivedDirectImage r).map
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
            (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Z.toRingedSpace)) 0).map e.hom) =
      (perfectHomComposition h g).hom.app ((schemeDerivedDirectImage f).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
          (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) 0).obj G)) ≫
        singleDegreeBaseChangeComposite f (h ≫ g) p₀ r ho 0 G
